claims.text: An epitaxial FeCoNi–platinum-group-metal high-entropy-alloy shell will enhance the durability of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
The shell will stabilize the catalyst surface structure under reaction conditions.
The shell will tune the catalyst's surface electronic states.
Surface stabilization and electronic-state tuning will reduce deactivation caused by poisoning and degradation.
Epitaxial shell formation changes the catalyst's surface composition.
The shell-induced electronic changes optimize adsorption energies for ethanol.
The shell-induced electronic changes optimize adsorption energies for oxygen-containing species.
Optimized adsorption energies minimize the formation of poisoning intermediates.
Minimizing poisoning intermediates preserves catalytic active sites.
The shell protects the catalyst surface against degradation during prolonged ethanol oxidation.
Coated catalysts will show a slower decline in current density or turnover frequency than uncoated PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Improved activity retention will correlate with more stable surface electronic properties observed by operando XAS.
The hypothesized benefit applies only at temperatures, potentials, and pH values within the shell's stability limits.
The coating must be uniform to produce the anticipated electronic and structural modifications.
The coating must be epitaxially grown to produce the anticipated electronic and structural modifications.
Analogous studies in related catalyst systems have found that epitaxial shell deposition improves catalytic performance.
